propositions: The shutdown drain in app.py's lifespan awaits queue.join() only, which protects webhook-queued reviews but not reconciler in-flight reviews that call review_and_vote inline outside the queue.

When the webhook queue is empty, queue.join() returns immediately and the reconcile_loop task is cancelled within shutdown_cancel_seconds() (~10s), abandoning a backfill review that may take minutes to complete.
Any container stop path (manual docker compose restart, host reboot, systemd stop, autodeploy rollback) kills in-flight reconciler reviews silently with no effective drain budget.
The drain must accept a cooperative stop signal to prevent new reviews from starting during shutdown, ensuring the drain deadline is not extended indefinitely by newly queued work.
Both webhook queue and reconciler in-flight reviews must share a single shutdown_drain_seconds() deadline to maintain the existing relationship with stop_grace_period.
